subtitles.en: And so we do have to think differently because the strategies that sort of got us into this mess the sort of ways in which we are facing so many challenges they're not going to be the same challenges that get us out.
subtitles.zh: 所以我们必须换一种思路，因为让我们陷入困境的策略，面对诸多挑战的方式，不会成为让我们脱困的答案。

subtitles.en: And I think for those that have been showing up in this moment protesting raising their voices in different ways they're asking a lot of times of like why are we losing?
subtitles.zh: 我想对那些此刻站出来抗议、以不同方式发声的人说，他们常常问：为什么我们一直在输？

subtitles.en: Why haven't we won more things? And the answer accountability?
subtitles.zh: 为什么我们没有赢得更多？答案是问责吗？

subtitles.en: Well the answer is that we've just been using the wrong strategies. The answer is that we haven't had a clear analysis around where we take the fights to.
subtitles.zh: 答案是，我们一直在用错误的策略。我们没有清晰分析该把斗争引向何处。

subtitles.en: And so I think that losing and recognizing that you're losing is like the first step on the way to winning.
subtitles.zh: 所以我认为，失败并认识到自己正在失败，是通往胜利的第一步。

subtitles.en: Because I think one thing that the right wing has done really effective is they've changed politics.
subtitles.zh: 因为我认为右翼做得非常有效的一件事是，他们改变了政治。

subtitles.en: They've made it so that everyone has a role. So people wear their red caps out in the world if you go into...
subtitles.zh: 他们让每个人都有角色。所以人们戴着红帽子出现在世界上，如果你走进……

subtitles.en: A tangible identity.
subtitles.zh: 一种有形的身份认同。

subtitles.en: Yeah they go into a gym they're changing the challenge of conservative media.
subtitles.zh: 是的，他们走进健身房，改变着保守派媒体的挑战。

subtitles.en: They're doing all sorts of things to shape the environment that they live in.
subtitles.zh: 他们做各种事情来塑造自己生活的环境。

subtitles.en: And a lot of times for folks who believe in social change and progress are almost whispering their beliefs or maybe just showing up to a protest in the most comfortable part of town.
subtitles.zh: 很多时候，相信社会变革和进步的人们几乎是在低声细语地表达信念，或者只是出现在城里最舒适的地方参加抗议。

subtitles.en: You know on the designated day where it gets wrapped up after three hours and everyone goes home but then the rest of their time they're not wearing their energy out in the world.

clips.title: 拉沙德·罗宾逊：与扎克伯格交锋，我学到了“对话”与“谈判”的区别

subtitles.en: How did you think about the dynamic that you had and representing people who had real grievances and wanted real change with folks who'd really reached the session on where they hadn't been thinking about that very much?
subtitles.zh: 你如何看待这种动态：你代表有真实不满、想要真正改变的人们，与那些已经达到一定地位、却不太考虑这些的人打交道？

subtitles.en: So I tell a lot of stories in the book about this because I think it's really important to unlock for folks what happens behind the scenes because some of these lessons of going in and trying to push Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg at Facebook to do something different.
subtitles.zh: 我在书中讲了很多这样的故事，因为我认为让人们了解幕后发生的事情非常重要。这些教训包括走进Facebook，试图推动马克·扎克伯格和谢丽尔·桑德伯格做出改变。

subtitles.en: What you were doing is yes and getting and getting change is actually similar to like going into your school board meeting or going into your local library board or whatever.
subtitles.zh: 你所做的，以及获得改变，实际上类似于参加学校董事会会议或当地图书馆董事会会议等。

subtitles.en: And you know one of the things I learned in those back and forth.
subtitles.zh: 在这些来回交锋中，我学到的一件事是……

subtitles.en: Well first of all my first meeting where we finally built up enough leverage to go and meet with Mark and Sheryl after there was a lot of back and forth in the media and they had hired a PR firm to attack me in the organization.
subtitles.zh: 首先，我的第一次会议，我们终于建立了足够的杠杆去与马克和谢丽尔会面，此前媒体上有很多来回，他们还雇了公关公司攻击我和我的组织。

subtitles.en: I get to Menlo Park and they want me to sign an NDA and I was like not signing an NDA so they give me a big back to says NDA on it that I have to wear around the campus.
subtitles.zh: 我到了门洛帕克，他们想让我签保密协议，我说不签，于是他们给了我一个背后写着NDA的大牌子，我必须戴着它在园区里走动。

subtitles.en: But because I didn't sign that NDA I'm actually tell real stories about what happened and one of the things I learned was the difference between being in a dialogue and negotiating.
subtitles.zh: 但因为我没有签那份保密协议，我才能讲述真实发生的故事。我学到的一件事是“对话”和“谈判”之间的区别。

subtitles.en: Your opponents want to keep you in a dialogue. They want to say we're talking to that group. We've heard those clive and activists.
subtitles.zh: 你的对手想让你停留在对话中。他们想说：我们正在和那个团体谈，我们听到了那些活动人士的声音。

subtitles.en: We've heard the women that are upset about this and we're listening to them and we're really concerned.
subtitles.zh: 我们听到了对此不满的女性，我们在倾听，我们真的很关心。

subtitles.en: When you have it when you're in negotiation you have leverage. You have the ability to actually move something but knowing the difference between whether just in a conversation that feels good and whether or not you have the ability to actually make meaningful change is the difference between presence and power.
subtitles.zh: 当你处于谈判中时，你有杠杆，你有能力真正推动事情。但知道是仅仅进行一场感觉良好的对话，还是拥有真正做出有意义改变的能力，这就是“在场”和“权力”的区别。

subtitles.en: And far too often we can be incentivized to want to be in the room. We want to be incentivized to feel like we've been shouted out or our concerns have been amplified but those are not the same as actually moving things along.
subtitles.zh: 很多时候，我们被激励着想要进入那个房间，想要感觉自己的声音被听到，担忧被放大，但这些并不等同于真正推动事情前进。

clips.speaker: Rashad Robinson
clips.title: 登个结婚启事：也能，改变观念？

subtitles.en: I hear a lot it's not on me to educate you and that's completely fair but it also might be counterproductive.
subtitles.zh: 我常听到“教育你不是我的责任”，这完全合理，但也可能适得其反。

subtitles.en: I write a lot about this because between 2005 and 2011 I was ahead of programs that glad and did a lot of work in Hollywood and in local communities and I tell a story centered on the culture of belief.
subtitles.zh: 我写了很多关于这个的内容，因为2005年到2011年间，我负责一些项目，在好莱坞和当地社区做了很多工作，我讲了一个以“信念文化”为中心的故事。

subtitles.en: Back 2006 I remember going to places like Alabama and deep red parts of Texas and training couples to both tell their stories but also start putting their wedding announcements in the newspaper
subtitles.zh: 记得2006年，我去过阿拉巴马州和得克萨斯州深红地区，培训情侣们讲述他们的故事，并开始把结婚启事登在报纸上。

subtitles.en: long before marriage equality was a thing and forcing advocating to have newspapers except those same sex wedding announcements right because what we knew from the research at the time is that more people once they knew gay and lesbian couples once where they were like around them they're not another.
subtitles.zh: 早在婚姻平等成为议题之前，我们就推动报纸接受同性结婚启事。因为当时的研究告诉我们，一旦人们认识同性恋伴侣，知道他们就在身边，他们就不再是“另类”。

subtitles.en: Yes but we also saw that people weren't talking about their lives they may come out and then after that they weren't having conversations with the straight people in their lives so people weren't being invested.
subtitles.zh: 是的，但我们也看到人们不谈论自己的生活，他们可能出柜了，但之后并没有与生活中的异性恋者进行对话，所以人们没有被“投入”其中。

subtitles.en: And so understanding from a strategic lens is like you know the thing that's actually going to change people's hearts and minds it's folks talking about it and engage but people are not talking about it and engage and now you know from a strategic lens you have to shift sort of how people are showing up.
subtitles.zh: 从战略角度看，真正能改变人们观念的是大家谈论和参与，但人们没有这样做。所以从战略上，你必须改变人们出现的方式。
en_highlights: shift how people are showing up

subtitles.en: And so I do think the like culture of belief of people being willing to stand up and take risk even when they don't know what's on the other side because the people who were putting their same sex wedding announcements in the newspaper in 2006 could have had their announcement in the paper on a Sunday and then show up on a Monday and be legally fired from their job for it and so that is a risk they could be legally ostracized and so every social movement has been built by people willing to take deep risk
subtitles.zh: 所以我确实认为，信念文化让人们愿意站出来冒险，即使不知道结果如何。因为2006年把同性结婚启事登报的人，可能周日登报，周一就被合法解雇，这就是风险，他们可能被合法排斥。每个社会运动都是由愿意承担深度风险的人建立的。

subtitles.en: and at the same time movements have to be thoughtful about where we're directing people's energy right it's not enough to just say show up here or protest here if you don't have a theory about sort of what are we trying to do what's our leverage what's our power.
subtitles.zh: 同时，运动必须深思熟虑地引导人们的能量。仅仅说“到这里来”或“在这里抗议”是不够的，除非你有理论：我们要做什么？我们的杠杆是什么？我们的权力是什么？

subtitles.en: And then the price was getting high as what Eiger told me. And at some point, a little birdie or an intermediary suggested or told Bob Eiger and Josh Kushner, hey, you should go look at the Lakers.
subtitles.zh: 艾格告诉我，当时价格越抬越高。后来有内部消息人士或中间人建议他们：不如去看看湖人队。

subtitles.en: And sure enough that had to be on Saturday or Sunday. And some 72 hours later, maybe 90 hours later, they had to deal.
subtitles.zh: 果然，那大概是在周六或周日。大约72小时，也许90小时后，他们就达成了交易。

subtitles.en: They were looking in Vegas. They were going to start a team from scratch, Randall. What happened? I really think that there's a Walmart family involved, or a Walton family involved.
subtitles.zh: 他们原本在拉斯维加斯，打算从零开始组建球队。兰德尔，发生了什么？我认为沃尔玛家族，也就是沃尔顿家族参与其中。

subtitles.en: And there's a couple of other groups involved in Las Vegas, including GoFoli, who's the owner of the Golden Knights. And then you have Mark Lazarie and the group known as the Las Vegas Jacks.
subtitles.zh: 拉斯维加斯还有其他几个集团参与，包括金骑士队老板戈福利，还有马克·拉扎里及其团队，即拉斯维加斯杰克队。

subtitles.en: When you have that many groups involved, naturally, that competition is going to drive the price high. Now, Josh Kushner and Bob Eiger were considered favorites.
subtitles.zh: 这么多集团参与，竞争自然会推高价格。乔什·库什纳和鲍勃·艾格原本是热门人选。

subtitles.en: However, if they say it's high, I can only imagine that I would guesstimate that it's over $10 billion.
subtitles.zh: 不过，如果他们都觉得价格太高，我只能猜测，成交价可能超过100亿美元。

subtitles.en: Randall and I, we were at the New York Knicks Parade, so we did that together.
subtitles.zh: 兰德尔和我一起参加了纽约尼克斯队的游行，我们共同经历了那件事。

subtitles.en: We had a great time out there. But now all this, the Knicks moving closer to this New York Ranger spin-off, I mean, what's going on? Is this going through?
subtitles.zh: 我们在那里玩得很开心。但现在，尼克斯队与纽约游骑兵队分拆的计划越来越近，到底怎么回事？能成吗？

subtitles.en: I think so. I think the Knicks or Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation is targeting separating the Rangers business from the Knicks business.
subtitles.zh: 我觉得能成。尼克斯队，或者说麦迪逊广场花园体育公司，正计划将游骑兵队的业务从尼克斯队的业务中分离出来。

subtitles.en: And so what this will mean is that Madison Square Garden Sports Corporation will become the Madison Square Garden Knicks Corporation, and then there will be a separate Rangers business.
subtitles.zh: 这意味着麦迪逊广场花园体育公司将更名为麦迪逊广场花园尼克斯公司，而游骑兵队将成为独立的业务。

subtitles.en: What's expected to happen is this is going to extract value. This is going to figure out the difference between the Knicks business and the Rangers business.
subtitles.zh: 预计这将释放价值，厘清尼克斯业务与游骑兵业务之间的差异。

subtitles.en: And James Dolan has said that he has no plans of selling either team.
subtitles.zh: 詹姆斯·多兰表示，他没有出售任何一支球队的计划。

subtitles.en: But once you see the value of those teams, who's to say he couldn't get $2 billion for 20% of the team, or maybe even 15% of the team?
subtitles.zh: 但一旦这些球队的价值显现，谁能说他不能以20%的股份获得20亿美元，甚至15%的股份呢？

subtitles.en: You know what's interesting. I think the FT had a piece too. And we talked about this on air with David Weston, of course, formerly head of ABC News.
subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，金融时报也有一篇报道。我们之前和ABC新闻前负责人大卫·韦斯顿在节目中讨论过。

subtitles.en: He knows Bob Iger. But we were talking about this idea at Randall, and I'm curious what you guys are hearing.
subtitles.zh: 他认识鲍勃·艾格。我们正在讨论这个观点，兰德尔，我很好奇你们听到了什么。

subtitles.en: That the interest in sports teams kind of resilient to AI, artificial intelligence.
subtitles.zh: 人们对体育球队的兴趣似乎对人工智能具有韧性。

subtitles.en: As we think about it in a world where we don't know, I feel like a lot's going to be impacted. Sports, maybe not so much.
subtitles.zh: 在我们这个充满不确定性的世界里，我觉得很多领域都会受到影响，但体育可能不会。

subtitles.en: Live sports, sir. Yeah, I doubt it. I doubt it right now.
subtitles.zh: 现场体育，先生。是的，我怀疑它不会。我目前持怀疑态度。

subtitles.en: I think that AI will enhance sports experiences. You think about walking into a new arena.
subtitles.zh: 我认为AI会增强体育体验。想象一下走进一座新球馆。

subtitles.en: If you're a seasoned ticket holder, is your experience now customized? Do the arena or does your app say welcome back, Carol?
subtitles.zh: 如果你是资深季票持有者，你的体验是否已经个性化？球馆或你的应用会说：欢迎回来，卡罗尔？

subtitles.en: We'd love to have you eat the barbecue chicken you had last time. Sort of those customized experiences is what I expect.
subtitles.zh: 我们很高兴为您提供上次吃过的烤鸡。这种定制化体验正是我所期待的。

subtitles.en: Now, long term, if someone's able to create a technology based league, something with robots or something that I think is where far away from, that's the only threat that I see, but it's not in sight.
subtitles.zh: 长期来看，如果有人能创建一个基于技术的联赛，比如机器人什么的，我认为那还很遥远，那是我看到的唯一威胁，但目前还看不到。

subtitles.en: It's a fantasy. I got to ask you, are you okay?
subtitles.zh: 那只是幻想。我得问问你，你还好吗？

winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
